cards.body:
## Summary
The lab proved that a hint must be checked, not only asked, to withhold: the model assembled the answer 6/6 once it had the parts, and the checker itself had to learn that. Production kept the asking and dropped the checking on the hint path. This card makes the lab's oracle the one withholding rule on the hint path. It also makes that rule able to read an item the way a photographed page actually delivers it.

## Description
The leak rule exists three times: vision/poc_hints.py leaks (known answer), vision/poc_hints_es.py assembles (answer built from parts), and desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts leaks (substitution). Only the last is in the product, and it runs on one of the five model-written fields that reach the TV from maths help: the explain reply. The hint path, which is the PoC B pipeline itself, puts hint and next on screen and speaks the hint with no check at all. rules/maths leaks() could not help if it were wired in. It substitutes into the item, and a read page's item is 'Solve for x:  3x − 7 = 11'. verify() cannot lex the words, so the probe returns leaks = false for 'x = 6' on all 4 equation items of the corpus page. With the words stripped, it returns true for all 4. The structural move: rules/maths gains equationOf(itemText) and an expression form check (an equivalent product or polynomial, or a linear bracket whose root zeroes the expression: the PoC's '(x+3)', '(x+4)', 'x^2 + x - 12' leak terms, derived rather than hand-listed). leaks() reads through equationOf. hint() runs the gate on both fields, re-asks once and names the leak, and after a second leak falls back to a withheld line written in rules/maths. The decision stays in code, which is repo law. Scope, stated honestly: single-variable equations and one-variable expressions (Factor, Expand). Systems, word problems and slope items have no oracle in the product and stay unchecked. The English and essay hint subjects are out of scope.

## Flow
- A /api/hint request arrives; hint('maths', item.text) asks the model as today
- rules/maths withholds(item.text, line) runs on hint and on what_to_try_next
- if clean, the hint is returned as today (0 re-asks on the 24 recorded real hints)
- if leaked, one re-ask with 'your last hint gave the answer away; go one step, stop short'
- if it leaks again, the item's withheld line from rules/maths, next = ''
- the session, TV and speech receive the same Hint shape as before

## Expected impact
A child can no longer be shown or read out the answer on the hint screen when the model slips. That is the product's stance ('withholding is the product') and PoC B's kill criterion, now enforced in code instead of only requested in a prompt. The lab corpus in prototype/data.json becomes the rule's contract test, so a future prompt or engine change that starts leaking goes red in test:rules.

## Evaluation
Claim: every maths hint line bound for the TV passes one code-owned withholding rule that can read the item as the page gives it
Before: 0 of 5 non-guard acceptance cases pass (probe: leaks() catches 0 of 4 outright answers on the corpus page's equation items; 1 of 5 TV-bound maths model fields is checked)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

cards.body:
## Summary
Today, to learn whether the desk still does what the lab proved, an operator runs four Python scripts that exercise Python copies of the pipelines, reads their printouts by hand and compares them with a table in a doc. And the one thing production changed, item positions from the model and a tap picking the nearest one, was never measured at all. This card gives the operator one command, `npm run bench` in desk/. It runs the lab's corpus through the PRODUCTION read, hint and lesson-pick modules on whatever engine is registered, prints the PoC baseline beside this run's figure and a pass/fail per kill criterion, and exits non-zero on a fail.

## Description
The corpus is already in the tree. prototype/data.json holds the maths and essay sample pages the phone offers (md5-identical to desk/public/samples), with every item's printed text and photo-space centre, the 24 recorded maths hint stages and the run-3 lesson picks. tools/lab-corpus.cjs loads it and adds the small tables that live only in Python today: known answers and leak terms (poc_hints.py:26-39), and the 9 retrieval queries with their acceptable lesson ids or 'none' (poc_retrieval.py:42-52). The pipeline code is not copied. The bench calls desk's readPage, hint and pickLesson through the engines registry, so a result is a result about the product. The scorers are the lab's own, ported: equations_intact and sim (poc_ocr.py:198-211), leaks + assembles (poc_hints.py:87-98, poc_hints_es.py:157-162), and the right/none tally. One new measure: 'selects', meaning whether the phone's tap at an item's true centre picks that item, given the centres the model reported. To judge the rule the phone actually runs, the rule moves out of phone/page.tsx into a pure, client-safe lib/desk/select.ts, and both call it. Live mode is operator-only (Ollama/Claude/codex; DESK_TEXT_ENGINE=codex re-runs on codex, so two runs compare engines). --replay feeds recorded answers and is what the gate suite runs. The bench always runs with DESK_DATA_DIR in the OS temp dir. The phone and TV do not change.

## Flow
- `npm run bench` (or `-- --replay`, `-- --json`)
- read: sample pages -> readPage -> found / exact / selects / mean cy error, per page
- hints: 12 problems x 2 stages -> hint() -> leaked (lab rule), LaTeX in spoken fields, stage 2 repeating stage 1
- lessons: 9 queries -> pickLesson() -> right, including 'none' on the 2 out-of-library problems
- a table: pipeline | lab baseline | this run | provider | seconds, then a verdict per PoC kill criterion (STUDY-DESK-POC-RESULTS.md:7-9) and exit 0/1

## Expected impact
The lab stops being a snapshot from 7 September and becomes the yardstick the desk's pipelines are judged against, on the product's own code. The pending engine decision (Bedrock or codex for read and hint) gets a number instead of an impression. The first live run answers an open question: whether the model's item positions, which production trusts for every tap and every TV band, hold up the way the ring did (16/16).

## Evaluation
Claim: one command re-measures the lab's figures on the production pipelines and says pass/fail per kill criterion. The gate path is deterministic under replay
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the bench does not exist; the product's item selection has 0 measurements, and every baseline in POC-RESULTS was taken on Python copies)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: direction (a capability the vision-lab description does not name. It is inside the lab group's declared scope, 'Research code ... that inform the product')
